description: Title slide introducing the 25-slide simple explainer deck.

title: How does AI answer questions?
description: Simple 3-step RAG explanation: ask → search → answer. Like a student with an open-book exam.

title: What is a Knowledge Graph?
description: Dots (things) connected by lines (relationships). SVG diagram of a medical KG fragment.

title: Why is multi-hop reasoning so hard?
description: The 3-hop challenge: TCF7L2 → Type 2 Diabetes → Metformin. Why single-step search fails.

title: Paper 01: D-RAG — The Gap
description: What D-RAG figured out (joint training) and what's missing (flat ruler on curved road).

title: Paper 02: CogGRAG — The Gap
description: What CogGRAG figured out (verify each step) and what's missing (flat search underneath).

title: Paper 03: Goal-Oriented KG — The Gap
description: What Goal-KG figured out (exact queries) and what's missing (vocabulary mismatch).

title: Paper 04: M3KG-RAG — The Gap
description: What M3KG figured out (multimodal) and what's missing (separate flat spaces).

title: Paper 05: KG-RAG Wang — The Gap
description: What KG-RAG Wang figured out (dual channel) and what's missing (hops counted equally).

title: Paper 06: GraphFlow — The Gap
description: What GraphFlow figured out (flow matching) and what's missing (still Euclidean).

title: Paper 07: SG-RAG — The Gap
description: What SG-RAG figured out (full path retrieval) and what's missing (90% to 58% accuracy cliff).

title: Paper 08: HyKGE — The Gap
description: What HyKGE figured out (hypothesis first) and what's missing (exact match still needed). Correction: Hy = Hypothesis.

title: Paper 09: KRAGEN — The Gap
description: What KRAGEN figured out (step-by-step search) and what's missing (flat geometry each time).

title: Paper 10: KG2RAG — The Gap
description: What KG2RAG figured out (factual connections) and what's missing (breaks on sparse graphs).

title: They all have the same underlying flaw
description: Section divider summarizing all 10 gaps: every system treats hierarchical graphs as flat.

title: What is RMF-RAG? (Plain English)
description: The dome metaphor: general facts near center, specific facts near edge. Old way vs RMF-RAG way.

title: What is RMF-RAG? (Technical)
description: Poincaré ball embeddings, geodesic distance formula, D-RAG training loop preserved. geoopt implementation.

title: The Key Metaphor: GPS vs Straight Line
description: Euclidean distance = straight line through Earth. Geodesic = great circle arc. Same for knowledge graphs.

title: The Example Question
description: Setting up the 3-hop walkthrough: TCF7L2 gene → Type 2 Diabetes → Metformin.

title: Step 1: Place Everything in Hyperbolic Space
description: Embedding all KG entities in the Poincaré ball. TCF7L2 near the boundary (specific).

title: Step 2: Hop 1 — TCF7L2 to Type 2 Diabetes
description: First geodesic hop. How curved distance finds the right neighbor vs flat cosine.

title: Step 3: Hop 2 — Diabetes to Insulin Resistance
description: Second geodesic hop finding the bridge mechanism. Why bridge concepts matter.

title: Step 4: Hop 3 — Mechanism to Metformin
description: Third geodesic hop reaching the answer. Full 3-hop chain complete in the Poincaré ball.

title: Step 5: Generate the Answer
description: LLM receives the 4-fact chain and generates a grounded, complete, specific answer.

title: The Path Forward: HyperKG-RAG
description: 10-week plan, datasets, baselines, verdict: genuinely novel, publishable undergraduate research.
